# Egami.Formats.Extended: guide for coding agents

Egami.Formats.Extended reads and writes image formats that most apps never meet but some still need: PCX, SGI, Sun raster, XBM,
XPM, WBMP, Farbfeld, JPEG-LS and DDS textures (BC1 to BC7, mips, cube maps, arrays and volumes), reads KTX and KTX 2 textures and writes KTX 2 (BC1 to BC7, ETC1, ETC2, EAC, 2D ASTC LDR and HDR, Basis Universal ETC1S and UASTC, and uncompressed; Zstandard and zlib supercompressed), reads and writes DPX and Cineon film frames, and reads camera RAW (DNG, CR2, NEF, PEF, ARW, ORF, RW2 and RAF; CR3 previews and metadata), developed on
load. Each is a plugin on core Egami's public format API.

Namespaces: `Egami.Formats.Extended` (the `With...` methods), `Egami.Formats.Extended.<Format>` (`PcxFormat` and the other
format infos and options), with `Egami` and `Egami.Formats`.

## Egami's vocabulary

Egami has its own names. Use them, not names from other imaging libraries: Egami has no `Image` type, no `Mutate` or `Clone`
and no `Configuration`.

- `Raster` and `Raster<TPixel>` hold an image; `TPixel` is a pixel type such as `Rgba8`, `Rgb8`, `Gray8`, `Bgra8` or `RgbaF32`
  (namespace `Egami.Pixels`). `Raster.Load` returns the type that fits the file; `Raster.Load<Rgba8>` converts while decoding.
- `Raster.Probe` reads a file's size, format and orientation without decoding it.
- `Apply(ops => ...)` changes a raster in place through a chain of operations; `Derive(ops => ...)` returns a new raster.
  `As<TPixel>()` converts to a new raster and `Copy()` duplicates one.
- `Save(path)` picks the writer from the extension; `Save(stream, format, options)` names it. Loading always detects the format
  from the bytes, never from the extension.
- `EgamiContext` holds the settings, `SafetyLimits`, thread count and registered formats a call uses. It is immutable: change
  it with `with`, and pass it to `Load` or `Probe`, or make it the default once at startup with `EgamiContext.SetDefault`.
- Every `Raster` owns pooled pixel memory: dispose it, best with `using`. `Derive`, `As` and `Load` return new rasters that you
  dispose too.

## Entry points

- `WithExtendedFormats()`: every format in a context; `WithPcx()`, `WithSgi()`, `WithSunRaster()`, `WithXbm()`, `WithXpm()`,
  `WithWbmp()`, `WithFarbfeld()`, `WithJpegLs()`, `WithDds()`, `WithKtx()`, `WithKtx2()`, `WithDpx()`, `WithCineon()` and `WithRaw()` one at a time.
- DDS: Load gives mip 0 of the first surface; `DdsReaderOptions` (`Surface`, `MipLevel`, `IncludeMipLevels`,
  `ReconstructNormalZ`) and LoadAll reach every face, array slice, depth slice and mip; `DdsDetails` keeps the DXGI format.
  Save writes a full mip chain; `DdsWriterOptions` (`Format`, `MipLevels`, `Effort`, `Srgb`, `Cube`) and SaveAll write
  block formats, arrays and cube maps. Integer and depth formats write mip 0 alone by default.
- KTX and KTX 2: `KtxFormat` (read only) and `Ktx2Format` (read and write); `KtxReaderOptions` (`Surface`, `MipLevel`, `IncludeMipLevels`,
  `ReconstructNormalZ`, `KeepStoredLayout`) as DDS's; `KtxDetails` keeps the Vulkan or OpenGL format, supercompression,
  orientation, swizzle and key/value pairs. 3D ASTC, PVRTC, UASTC HDR 6 × 6, XUASTC and XUBC7 throw `UnsupportedFormatException`.
  `Ktx2WriterOptions` (`Format` a `KtxTextureFormat`, `MipLevels`, `Effort`, `Srgb`, `Cube`, `Supercompression`,
  `CompressionLevel`, `BasisQuality`, `UastcRdo`) writes uncompressed, BC, ETC, EAC, ASTC LDR, ETC1S and UASTC; no KTX 1.1
  writing, no ASTC HDR or UASTC HDR, no SNORM.
- `Texture` (`Egami.Formats.Extended.Textures`): `Texture.Load` a whole DDS, KTX or KTX 2 file; `GetImage`/`SetImage` by mip,
  layer, face and slice; `GenerateMips`, `TrimMips`; `Save` to .dds or .ktx2 with exactly its mips (volumes too).
- DPX and Cineon: `DpxFormat`, `CineonFormat`. Load gives the stored code values unchanged (10-bit RGB as `Rgb16`, code 1023
  at 65535); `DpxReaderOptions.Linearize` gives scene-linear `RgbF32` by Kodak's conversion (685 white, 95 black) for log
  elements; `DpxReaderOptions.Element` and LoadAll reach every image element. `DpxDetails` and `CineonDetails` keep the depth,
  packing, transfer and the file, film and TV fields (timecode, frame rate, slate), and the writers write them back.
  `DpxWriterOptions` (`BitsPerSample` 8, 10, 12 or 16, `BigEndian`, `Transfer`); Cineon writes 10-bit RGB only.
- RAW: Load develops a DNG into `Rgb16` sRGB (or straight into the RGB space `ConvertColorTo` names); `RawReaderOptions`
  (`Output` = `Developed`, `HalfSize`, `Preview` or `Mosaic`; `WhiteBalance`, `Temperature`, `Tint`, `Exposure`, `Demosaic`,
  `Highlights`, `LuminanceNoiseReduction`, `ColorNoiseReduction`, `LensCorrections`, `ApplyProfile`) sets it; `RawDetails`
  keeps the camera, sensor layout and the colour the develop used.
- JPEG-LS: `JpegLsFormat` (.jls, T.87) reads every interleave mode, 2 to 16 bits, palettes and HP colour transforms, and
  is detected ahead of JPEG. `JpegLsWriterOptions` (`Near`, `Interleave`, `ColorTransform`, `BitsPerSample`,
  `RestartInterval`); `JpegLsDetails` keeps NEAR, depth and interleave; `JpegLsWriter.Write` codes plain `ushort` samples
  (1 to 4 components), for DICOM and the like. No JPEG-LS part 2 (T.870).
- `EgamiContext.SetDefault(new EgamiContext().WithExtendedFormats())` at startup makes them work in every call.
- Load, Probe, streaming decodes, Save and Transcode then work as they do for core formats, inside the same safety limits.

## Samples

All of them:

```csharp
// Every stable format of Egami.Formats.Extended, once at startup before any other Egami call:
// EgamiContext.SetDefault(new EgamiContext().WithExtendedFormats());

// ...or in a context of its own.
EgamiContext context = EgamiContext.Default.WithExtendedFormats();
using Raster image = Raster.Load("duck.png", context);

// A raster saves to a path through the context it was loaded with, so the extension picks PCX.
image.Save("duck.pcx");
using Raster back = Raster.Load("duck.pcx", context);
string format = back.Metadata.FormatName!;               // "PCX"
```

One at a time:

```csharp
// One format at a time: each has its own method and its own FormatInfo.
EgamiContext context = EgamiContext.Default.WithSgi().WithSunRaster();
using (FileStream output = File.Create("duck.sgi"))
{
    image.Save(output, SgiFormat.Info);
}

RasterInfo info = Raster.Probe("duck.sgi", context);
Console.WriteLine($"{info.Format.Name} {info.Width}×{info.Height} {info.Layout.ChannelOrder}");
```

DDS surfaces and mips:

```csharp
// One surface and mip: cube face -Y (faces go +X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z), third mip.
using Raster face = Raster.Load("sky.dds", context, new DdsReaderOptions { Surface = 3, MipLevel = 2 });

// Every face at mip 0, or with every mip after its face.
using RasterList faces = Raster.LoadAll("sky.dds", context);
using RasterList all = Raster.LoadAll("sky.dds", context, new DdsReaderOptions { IncludeMipLevels = true });

// A thumbnail reads the smallest mip that still covers the size, a fraction of the file.
using Raster thumbnail = Raster.Load("sky.dds", context, new ReaderOptions { MinimumSize = new Size(8, 8) });

// Two-channel normal maps (BC5, R8G8) load with blue 0, or with Z rebuilt.
using Raster normals = Raster.Load("sky.dds", context, new DdsReaderOptions { ReconstructNormalZ = true });
```

KTX surfaces, mips and the stored layout:

```csharp
// One surface and mip: cube face -Y (faces go +X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z), second mip if it has one.
using Raster face = Raster.Load("sky.ktx2", context, new KtxReaderOptions { Surface = 3 });

// Every face at mip 0, or with every mip after its face.
using RasterList faces = Raster.LoadAll("sky.ktx2", context);
using RasterList all = Raster.LoadAll("texture.ktx2", context, new KtxReaderOptions { IncludeMipLevels = true });

// The pixels as the file stores them: no KTXorientation flip and no KTXswizzle.
using Raster stored = Raster.Load("texture.ktx2", context, new KtxReaderOptions { KeepStoredLayout = true });
```

DPX code values and linear light:

```csharp
// A printing-density (log) scan, converted to scene-linear light with Kodak's conversion:
// code 685 is 1.0 (white) and code 95 is 0.0 (black). Linear and video DPX files load unchanged.
using Raster<RgbF32> linear = Raster.Load<RgbF32>("scan.cin", context, new DpxReaderOptions { Linearize = true });
```

A RAW develop:

```csharp
RawReaderOptions develop = new()
{
    WhiteBalance = RawWhiteBalance.Custom,
    Temperature = 4800,                    // kelvin
    Tint = 5,                              // toward magenta
    Exposure = -0.5,                       // stops
    Highlights = RawHighlightMode.Rebuild, // recover clipped colour from what was not clipped
    Demosaic = RawDemosaicMethod.Malvar,   // faster than the default AHD
    LuminanceNoiseReduction = 20,          // 0 to 100; off by default
    ColorNoiseReduction = 40,              // 0 to 100; 25 by default
    AutoChromaticAberration = true,        // fix colour fringes when no lens profile covers the file
    DefaultToneCurve = true,               // a contrast curve like Adobe Camera Raw's default; off by default
    ConvertColorTo = Colors.ColorProfile.DisplayP3, // rendered straight into P3, the profile attached
};
using Raster photo = Raster.Load("photo.dng", context, develop);
photo.Save("photo-p3.png");
```

JPEG-LS, near-lossless and from plain samples:

```csharp
// Near-lossless: every sample within 2 of the original, for a much smaller file. Restart markers every 64 lines let a
// damaged file be read again from the next one.
using (FileStream near = File.Create("duck-near.jls"))
{
    duck.Save(near, JpegLsFormat.Info, new JpegLsWriterOptions { Near = 2, RestartInterval = 64 });
}

// Lossless with HP's colour transform, which shrinks most photographs further, sample-interleaved.
using (FileStream hp = File.Create("duck-hp1.jls"))
{
    duck.Save(hp, JpegLsFormat.Info, new JpegLsWriterOptions { ColorTransform = JpegLsColorTransform.Hp1, Interleave = JpegLsInterleave.Sample });
}

// 12-bit samples from a 16-bit raster, as medical images often store them.
using Raster<Gray16> scan = duck.As<Gray16>();
using (FileStream twelve = File.Create("scan-12.jls"))
{
    scan.Save(twelve, JpegLsFormat.Info, new JpegLsWriterOptions { BitsPerSample = 12 });
}
```

```csharp
// Samples straight from another source, such as a DICOM pixel data element: 2 components, 10 bits, 64 × 32.
ushort[] samples = new ushort[64 * 32 * 2];
for (int i = 0; i < samples.Length; i++)
{
    samples[i] = (ushort)((i * 37) % 1024);
}

using (FileStream output = File.Create("samples.jls"))
{
    JpegLsWriter.Write(output, samples, components: 2, width: 64, bitsPerSample: 10);
}
```

## Common mistakes

- Referencing the package and expecting `.pcx` and the others to load. Register them in the context you load with, or as the
  default before any other Egami call.
- Saving to a path with a context that lacks them. `Save(path)` picks the writer through the raster's context, so a raster loaded
  without the formats cannot save as .pcx by extension; pass the format info (`PcxFormat.Info`) or load with the context.
- Expecting a DDS cube map or array to load whole with Load: it gives one surface. Use LoadAll, or `DdsReaderOptions.Surface`.
- Expecting a KTX texture written bottom-up (`KTXorientation` `ru`) to load bottom-up: Load turns it upright and applies
  `KTXswizzle`; `KtxReaderOptions.KeepStoredLayout` keeps the stored rows and channels.
- Expecting BC5 normal maps to have blue: it loads as 0 unless `DdsReaderOptions.ReconstructNormalZ` is set.
- Expecting a RAW load to turn the image upright: like every Egami load it returns the pixels as stored; `AutoOrient` turns
  them by `RasterInfo.Orientation`.
- Registering RAW with `WithFormat(RawFormat.Info)`: that puts it after TIFF, which then claims every DNG. Use `WithRaw()`.
- Expecting a DPX or Cineon scan to load as linear light: Load gives the log code values; set `DpxReaderOptions.Linearize`.
- Ignoring `Warnings` after a lenient read of a damaged file: it keeps what decoded and says what it recovered from.
